svg.title: macOS · Capture · Interval · Ladder running, stepped by hand · 960×720 sheet
svg.desc:
Mirrors App/CaptureView.swift (landscapeLayout → landscapeIntervalRow's running branch: intervalRunningPills, holyGrailReadout's ladder-only branch, ladderRunningRungDial; ladderViewfinderOverlays → LadderRail) with App/LightLadderViews.swift (LadderRail) on the macOS capture sheet. Drawn from the Debug build's window buffer on 2026-09-03 (LL_CAPTURE=1 LL_LADDER=running, which stages the Mac-truthful state: 823 outputs, 41 min in, Dusk). The live image is indicative — the build had no camera grant.
WHAT DIFFERS FROM THE PHONE'S RUNNING STATE (../iOS/capture-interval.ladder-running.portrait.svg): (1) THE READOUT'S THIRD LINE STANDS ALONE. The phone's readout leads with the ramp's exposure pair ("1/8 · ISO 1250", "scene EV 5.2 · 823 frames") and puts the ladder line under them; a Mac run has no ramp and so no HolyGrailState, and holyGrailReadout's ladder-only branch draws "Dusk · every 2 s · blend 3" by itself — the rung's pacing as asked, no governor note (there is no processing governor on the JPEG path). (2) A RUNG DIAL UNDER THE READOUT (ladderRunningRungDial): the same captioned pull-down the armed row carries — "RUNG · Dusk", menu Daylight · Fading · Dusk ✓ · Night — is how the operator steps the running ladder. Picking a rung calls CameraController.setLadderRung, which hands the rung's interval and blend depth to the live blend controller for the NEXT window (never the one in flight — the rule the phone's boundary step keeps), republishes LadderState, appends a line to Logs/ladder-<run>.jsonl (sceneEV null, changed true, no yieldedBy) and so moves the rail and fires the "Stepped down to Night" toast. It sits in the dial-row slot, outside the viewfinder's swipe and pinch gestures, because a menu placed on the rail — inside them — did not reliably open from a click. (3) THE RAIL IS PICTURE on every platform: one bar per rung with heights proportional to the ladder's EV spans (Daylight 3 · Fading 5 · Dusk 4 · Night 6 of the 16 … −2 drawing window → 30 · 50 · 40 · 60 pt of 180), the active rung widened to 22 pt and ringed in amber, its name in a chip beside it; allowsHitTesting(false). The Mac's LadderState carries no smoothedEV, so the rail's thresholds are the table's, not a meter's.
Unchanged from the phone: the run pills (the burst indicator's bar and count, the elapsed clock), the toast (3 s, "Stepped down to Night"), and the rest of the sheet's chrome (see capture-interval.ladder.svg). The RUNG menu itself is a system menu and is mirrored as a note in INDEX.md.
svg.text: macOS · Capture · Interval · Ladder running, stepped by hand · 960×720 sheet · 1 unit = 1 pt
Readout is the rung's line alone (no ramp) · RUNG dial steps the run from the next window · rail is picture
